proposals.title: Prescribe → Verify → Report: the clinician-owned prescription as the product's spine
proposals.one_liner: Flip the product from a patient app that a physio occasionally receives a PDF from into a clinician-prescribed, dose-verified home-delivery instrument: the physio enters the prescription (exercises, sides, dose in minutes/day and days/week, red-flag disposition) in a 5-minute portal, the app delivers exactly that and nothing else, and the physio gets a between-visit ledger of verified minutes vs prescribed, pain/PSFS, apex ATR (MDC-gated) and any safety event — so the physio, not the patient, is the one who insists on it.
proposals.why_100x: Mechanism, not adjectives: (1) Distribution flips from B2C one-at-a-time to one clinician = every patient on their list. A PSSE physio or a scoliosis clinic carries 50-300 active patients; one adopting clinician is worth more than a year of consumer acquisition, and adherence to a clinician-mandated tool is far higher than to a self-downloaded coach. (2) It answers the one question every scoliosis clinician cannot answer today and cares about most: 'did they actually do the 30-45 min/day, and at what dose?' PSSE only shows Cobb effects in trials at a stated home dose (the digest cites Schreiber 2015/2016: 30-45 min/day; Yuan 2025: 30 min/day, 5+ days/week) and home adherence is the known failure point of the whole method; a physio who can see 'prescribed 210 min/week, verified 95, self-reported 160, side plank done 11 of 14 days' changes what they do at the next visit. That is workflow value, which is what makes a clinician write 'use Balance' on the prescription. (3) It structurally deletes the product's largest confirmed clinical-risk class. Nearly every critical finding in the audit (sitting_waist_fold backwards, 'lean side' laterality inversion, X-ray photo convexity flips, absolute-tier folk contraindications, invented cascades, no fusion/brace/maturity handling) exists because the product is guessing the clinician's decisions from lay input. When the physio states the pattern, the sides, the exercises, the dose, the fusion/brace/maturity status and their own contraindication list, the self-guided inference layer becomes a fallback for the unreferred adult, not the core. The clinician's stated convexity overrides self-report; the clinician's exercise list replaces the library's side-keying; the clinician's dose becomes the adherence denominator. (4) It makes the CUHK/trial claim true instead of aspirational: a prescription snapshot plus provenance-flagged adherence events (form_check_verified | timer_only | chat_self_report) is exactly the per-protocol denominator a trial statistician needs, which is the digest's own conclusion about what the 'trial that can finally tell whether the exercise was done' pitch requires. (5) It unlocks a payer: clinics and insurers/pilots pay for remote monitoring and adherence data; patients rarely pay for exercise reminders. The product stops being 'an exercise app for scoliosis' and becomes 'the delivery-and-verification layer for prescribed PSSE', which is a category with a buyer.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: Directly reusable: (a) physio_cleared mode in lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts already treats the physio programme as authoritative; it just needs to become the ONLY path when a clinician is linked, and to consume a structured prescription instead of regex on LLM-normalised names. (b) /api/parse-program + lib/prompts/parseProgram.ts already turns pasted text into a ParsedProgram mapped to library ids: this becomes the clinician's paste-to-prefill step (they confirm, not the patient). (c) The liaison agent + liaison_documents/appointments tables (app/api/agents/liaison/route.ts) already assemble a per-appointment handoff from observations; it becomes a weekly clinician-facing ledger rather than a one-off PDF. (d) lib/agents/context.ts AdherenceSnapshot, lib/session/persist.ts exercises_completed and the per-rep form scores in lib/exercises/formCheck/* give the raw material for a provenance-flagged adherence event; toolFlagSafety and lib/safety/redFlags.ts give the safety-event stream to surface to the clinician. (e) lib/outcomes/compute.ts (PSFS, side-bridge, Sorensen) and lib/pose/repeatability.ts (MDC machinery) plus lib/atr/compute.ts give the outcome columns; atrPairsFrom already collects the pairs the MDC gate needs. (f) app/care-team/page.tsx is a ready scaffold for a clinician dashboard (programs, observations, appointments, documents are already fetched). (g) Supabase auth and the privacy/redaction layer (lib/privacy, agents never see names) extend naturally to a clinician role with patient linking.
proposals.what_it_needs: Engineering: clinician role + consent-gated patient linking (invite code or QR at the visit); a Prescription object as first-class data (exerciseId or clinician's own free exercise, side enum left|right|both, sets/reps/seconds, minutesPerDay, daysPerWeek, clinician-stated curve pattern and convex sides, fusion/brace/maturity flags, clinician's own do-not-do list, valid-from/until) snapshotted weekly; adherence event schema with provenance and formScore, with weekly verified and reported adherence computed against the snapshot; clinician weekly ledger view + per-patient CSV export; clinician-owned exercise media (their own video or the library's) so Schroth/SEAS-certified physios are not forced into Balance's Tier-3 wording; hard rule that side-keyed library cues are withheld unless clinician-stated (kills the laterality problem); safety-event routing to the linked clinician with the existing condition-free copy; Traditional Chinese for both sides. Clinical: 2-3 design-partner PSSE physios (HK and one Schroth/SEAS-certified clinic) to co-design the 5-minute prescription flow; a clinician sign-off on every remaining self-guided cue (the audit's ask) so the fallback path is not a liability that scares clinicians away from the linked path. Data: fix the denominator first (prescribed dose stored), then instrument verified vs reported minutes; expect form-check-verified to be honest only for side plank sag and rep counting per the biomech audit, so the primary verified signal is timer-on-exercise-screen plus rep count, labelled as such. Partnerships: CUHK orthopaedics/physio (docs/cuhk-approach.md already points here) for a monitoring-arm pilot; a HK physio association or two private scoliosis clinics as the first paying accounts. Regulatory/ethics: once a clinician relies on the ledger it is a clinical decision-support tool; expect PDPO data-processing agreements with clinics, an REB submission for the CUHK arm, and to keep all claims to adherence/pain/function/endurance (never curve change) so it stays in the lowest software-as-medical-device risk tier.
proposals.biggest_risk: Clinician non-adoption due to friction and liability, producing a two-sided cold start where neither side has data. Concretely: a physio will not type a prescription into a fourth system for no fee, and a physio who does will stop if the ledger creates alarms they must act on (a red-flag event at 9pm, a 'below prescribed dose' banner) without a reimbursement or workflow slot to absorb it. The second-order failure is that if the 'verified' signal degrades to timer-only (which the biomech audit says is likely for most exercises from a single webcam), the ledger is only modestly more trustworthy than a paper diary, and a sceptical clinician will discount it; if that happens the product has spent its runway building a portal for a signal clinicians do not believe. Mitigations, not guarantees: paste-to-prefill so the prescription takes under 5 minutes; default ledger is weekly digest with no interruptive alerts except the emergency tier; label verified vs reported honestly from day one; run the first pilot inside a clinic that already wants adherence data for a study, so the clinician's motive is the trial, not the app.
proposals.evidence_basis: High confidence (verified in code today): physio_cleared mode flags and never blocks; exerciseContraindicated() excludes nothing; /api/parse-program sends raw pasted text to Groq and matches against libraryForPrompt(); the liaison route generates a per-appointment PDF from unconsumed observations; app/care-team is an admin view with no clinician auth; no Prescription/dose object exists, so adherence has no denominator; exercises_completed mixes chat self-report and camera-verified entries with no provenance (per the evidence audit). High confidence (confirmed audit): nearly all critical/major clinical findings stem from lay-inferred sides, patterns and contraindications that a clinician could state directly. Medium confidence: the trial dose figures (Schreiber 2015/2016 30-45 min/day; Yuan 2025 30 min/day, 5+ days/week) and the 'adherence = delivered/prescribed, often >=80% per-protocol' convention are taken from the embedded digest and my clinical training; I did not re-verify the papers against a source in this run. Medium-to-low confidence: the claim that clinicians will mandate a tool that shows verified dose is an inference from PSSE practice (home dose is the known weak link) and from adjacent remote-therapeutic-monitoring products, not from user interviews with HK scoliosis physios; the panel-size and adoption multipliers are order-of-magnitude reasoning, not measured. Low confidence: regulatory tiering and any payer willingness in HK were not checked against current HK MDD or insurer guidance.
proposals.time_to_first_value: 6-8 weeks to a minimal linked mode with 2-3 design-partner physios: clinician magic-link login, paste-to-prefill prescription with sides and dose, self-guided path disabled for linked patients, weekly ledger (verified vs reported minutes, pain, PSFS, red-flag events) as a web page plus the existing PDF, CSV export. The first 'value moment' is the first follow-up visit where a physio changes a plan because of the ledger, realistically 3-4 weeks after the first patient is linked, so about 3 months from start. A CUHK monitoring-arm pilot with MDC-gated ATR and ICC on the adherence signal is 6-9 months and depends on REB timing.

proposals.title: Recorded With Your Physio: the patient's own supervised session becomes the programme, and the physio sees it happen
proposals.one_liner: At the appointment, the physio uses Balance to film the patient doing each exercise correctly under their hands (patient's own body, correct side, physio's voice cue, dose); that capture replaces the generic library as the home programme, each home session is verified against the patient's own clinic reference, and the physio gets a 30-second weekly view with a one-tap reply — so at week 26 the patient is still doing "my exercises, that my physio watches", not "an app's exercises".
proposals.why_100x: Three mechanisms, all about what kills adherence at week 6-10 for a scoliosis patient. (1) Fidelity: PSSE is individualised per curve and patients forget or drift the cues within days of leaving clinic; a paper handout or a generic library cannot encode "your left scapula, your right pelvis, that much breath". A video of the patient's own body in the corrected position, with the physio's own voice saying the cue they used in the room, is the highest-fidelity home prescription possible and needs no side-inference at all — laterality is baked in by the clinician who positioned the patient. This deletes at one stroke the entire class of audited harms (sitting_waist_fold inverted, bulge/lean self-report, X-ray laterality flips, invented hip-flexor rule, cascade chains): in this mode the product never has to decide which side is concave. (2) Accountability with a face: the strongest known lever on home-exercise adherence is feedback from the treating clinician, not gamification or an LLM persona. The retention engine becomes "my physio saw Tuesday's session and said 'good, hold the breath longer'". The Companion nudges become the physio's words, delivered by the app. (3) It changes who the customer is and what the product IS: from a consumer coach with a library a clinician distrusts, to the fidelity-and-adherence infrastructure of an existing clinical relationship. The buyer becomes the PSSE clinic (in HK, certified Schroth physios are scarce, private, seen roughly monthly, and currently hand out paper) and the trial group (CUHK's exact unmet need per docs/cuhk-approach.md: objective adherence to a therapist-defined prescription — now with the prescription itself captured as the reference, so 'did they do what was prescribed, how well' is finally answerable). Every physio who adopts brings all their scoliosis patients; the physio, not the founder, does the acquisition and the safety sign-off. Self-guided mode shrinks to a symmetric mobility/breathing fallback, which is the only place the current library is defensible anyway.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on:
- physio_cleared mode and the physio_programs table (lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts, supabase/schema.sql:41): the concept 'physio prescription is authoritative' already exists; today it is a pasted text list. Replace the text with structured items each carrying a clinic-captured video, a voice cue, a side (set by the physio), and dose.
- appointments + liaison_documents + Liaison agent (schema.sql:218-246, lib/agents/prompts.ts LIAISON_SYSTEM_PROMPT): the Liaison handoff already runs 24h before an appointment; invert it into a weekly physio-facing digest and reuse the appointment as the capture moment.
- notifications/inbox as record of truth with the 'documents never leave the platform' policy (lib/messaging/deliver.ts, app/inbox/page.tsx): the physio's replies land here; the mirror rule already protects clinical content.
- MediaPipe form-check engines with a baseline-stability phase (lib/exercises/formCheck/*, BASELINE_MOVEMENT_TOLERANCE): repurpose to extract the patient's own landmark geometry from the clinic capture and compare home reps to that personal reference in body-relative units, which is what the biomech audit asked for instead of frame-fraction thresholds. Keep only the 'plausible' checks (side-plank line, rep counting, T-stretch knee, hold timers).
- Session persistence and adherence context (lib/session/persist.ts, lib/agents/context.ts AdherenceSnapshot) — extend with the provenance schema the evidence audit specified (form_check_verified | timer_only | chat_self_report) so the physio digest and the trial export are the same data.
- care-team page (app/care-team/page.tsx) is already a multi-panel portfolio view; it becomes the physio's patient list.
- lib/tts.ts: swap synthetic voice for the physio's recorded cue.
- Supabase RLS already enabled on every table; add a clinician role linked to a patient by explicit consent.
proposals.what_it_needs: Engineering: clinician account + patient-link consent + RLS policies; an in-clinic capture flow that takes under 8 minutes for a 5-exercise programme (per exercise: 15-30s video, 10s voice cue, side, sets/reps/seconds; one tap to save) with encrypted storage and retention rules; home-session playback of the patient's own clip as the reference (side-by-side or ghost overlay); form-check refactor to compare against the personal clinic reference instead of fixed thresholds, with the 'theatre' checks removed; adherence event schema with provenance; a physio weekly digest (one screen: adherence vs prescribed dose, pain, ATR at the known apex level, form flags) with one-tap replies ('keep going', 'longer hold', 'come in early') and a voice-note reply; a 'your physio saw this' marker on the patient side. Clinical: two or three certified Schroth/SEAS physios as design partners to co-author the capture flow and the digest, and to sign off that a filmed-in-clinic reference is acceptable as the home prescription; a defined escalation path so the red-flag screen routes to the named physio, not only to a PDF. Data/ethics: video of patients' backs (including minors) — HK PDPO compliance, guardian consent and child assent, retention and deletion policy, data-minimisation statement; a small before/after study of week-12 and week-26 adherence against the current library path. Partnerships: one HK private physio clinic for the paid pilot (billable 'between-visit monitoring'), and the CUHK PWH physiotherapy group as the trial-instrument route already sketched in docs/cuhk-approach.md.
proposals.biggest_risk: The physio does not spend the minutes. Capture adds time to an appointment that already runs over, and the weekly review is unpaid work; if the physio stops looking, the patient discovers within two weeks that nobody is watching, and the accountability mechanism inverts — a 'seen by your physio' promise that goes unmet is worse for week-26 retention than no promise at all. This is a business-model risk as much as a UX one: it works only where monitoring is billable (private HK clinics) or funded (a trial), and the digest must be genuinely 30 seconds with a one-tap reply, or it dies. Secondary risks: filming adolescents' backs raises safeguarding and body-image issues that the current product does not yet handle (no age capture, no guardian consent — see the safety_informatics findings), and any patient without a physio still falls back to the generic library, so the audited library and laterality fixes remain mandatory, not superseded.
proposals.evidence_basis: Confidence by claim. HIGH: PSSE methods (Schroth, SEAS, BSPTS) are individualised to curve pattern and delivered by trained therapists, and the only trials with Cobb effects used that supervised, method-specific delivery (Schreiber 2015/2016 as already cited in the evidence audit); a clinician-positioned reference removes the app's need to infer laterality, which is the root of the critical library and profile findings. MEDIUM (from general physiotherapy literature, not scoliosis-specific, and not re-verified against sources in this run): home-exercise adherence falls off within weeks and is over-reported by diaries; feedback and supervision from the treating clinician are among the strategies most consistently associated with better adherence in reviews of physiotherapy home-programme adherence; patients recall prescribed exercises poorly and video-based instruction improves performance accuracy over paper handouts. MEDIUM: certified Schroth physiotherapists in Hong Kong are few and private, with roughly monthly visits — from domain familiarity, not a counted source. LOW/UNTESTED: that a physio will reliably review a weekly digest — no evidence in the codebase or literature I can cite; this is precisely the pilot's primary hypothesis. Internal evidence: docs/cuhk-approach.md already identifies objective adherence to a therapist-defined prescription as the product's only genuinely differentiated asset; this feature is the shortest path to making that claim true.
proposals.time_to_first_value: 4-6 weeks for the founder-and-her-own-physio pilot: physio films the exercises on a phone in clinic, the app plays the patient's own clip as the session reference with timer and hold, no form-check, physio receives the existing Liaison digest re-cut as a weekly note. 2-3 months for the clinician role, capture flow and one-tap reply with two partner physios and 10-20 patients. A first retention read (week-12 adherence, recorded-with-physio vs library path) at about 5-6 months; the week-26 answer at about 8 months. The CUHK conversation can begin as soon as the capture plus provenance-tagged adherence export exist, roughly month 3.

proposals.title: Trial Mode: a locked-prescription, dose-denominated, provenance-tagged adherence instrument with statistician-grade export
proposals.one_liner: Turn Balance from a coach that prescribes into an instrument that measures: the clinician's PSSE prescription becomes a versioned, signed object; every set is logged as an adherence event with prescribed-vs-completed dose and a source tag (form-check-verified | timer-only | chat-self-report); the LLM coach, self-guided programme generator, cascade models and scan-trend language are switched OFF in this mode; and the whole thing exports as a pseudonymised per-participant table with a data dictionary a trial statistician can drop into a per-protocol analysis.
proposals.why_100x: The multiplier is a change of buyer and a change of what the artefact is worth per user. Today the product's value per user is one patient's exercise habit, and the audit shows that as a prescriber it is currently net-negative (backwards waist-fold cue, invented cascades, a contraindication engine that flags physio programmes and blocks nothing). As a trial instrument, value per user is a fraction of the cost of the trial it makes interpretable: every PSSE RCT (Schreiber-style, 6 months, 30-45 min/day home dose) has the same unsolved confound - if the exercise arm underperforms nobody can say whether the exercise failed or was not done, because adherence is a paper diary. docs/cuhk-approach.md already names this as "the only part of this product genuinely ahead of what a research group could commission" but the code does not deliver it: exercises_completed has no denominator, no timestamps per set, mixes chat self-report with camera-verified reps, and the prescription is never snapshotted. Mechanism, step by step: (1) a locked prescription gives adherence a denominator, so weekly adherence = verified minutes / prescribed minutes exists for the first time; (2) the source tag lets a statistician run per-protocol analysis on verified dose and sensitivity analysis on reported dose - that is the analysis nobody in PSSE research can currently run, and it yields the first dose-response data in the field; (3) switching off every prescribing/coaching component in Trial Mode converts the audit's liabilities into non-issues (the physio's prescription is authoritative, the app adds no co-intervention that would confound the trial arm) and drops the regulatory posture from "software that prescribes exercise" to "software that records exercise"; (4) a trial that designs the instrument into its protocol produces a peer-reviewed paper citing it, which is the validation every clinician demands before recommending it to patients - so the research angle is also the only credible route back to the consumer/clinic market; (5) the same ledger, once a few hundred patient-years exist, is the longitudinal behaviour-plus-pain-plus-ATR dataset the roadmap's TOCI/progression conversation needs. One instrument, three markets (trials, PSSE clinics, then patients), and the trial market pays in credibility rather than cash, which is what this product is actually short of.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: lib/session/persist.ts already writes a Supabase sessions row keyed by profile_id with started_at/completed_at/pain_check/exercises_completed - the ledger is an expansion of exerciseSummaries into per-set events, not a new pipeline. lib/exercises/formCheck/* produce per-rep form scores and compensation events that are computed but never persisted; the rep counters for hip bridge/lunge and the side-plank hold timer are the pieces the biomech audit rates PLAUSIBLE, which is exactly what "verified" should be built on. lib/prompts/parseProgram.ts + selectProgram physio_cleared mode already ingest a pasted physio programme with source_text - that is the prescription object, missing only versioning, sets/reps/minutes-per-day/days-per-week fields, a clinician signature and a lock. lib/pose/repeatability.ts has SEM/MDC95/Bland-Altman and buildMdcTable, and lib/atr atrPairsFrom collects test-retest pairs - the instrument's own reliability study is mostly written. lib/outcomes/compute.ts (PSFS, Sorensen, side-bridge L/R) are the secondary outcomes a trial would want alongside adherence. lib/agents/tools.ts log_exercise already writes to exercises_completed with a source column ("real") - the provenance enum slots straight in. scripts/check-safety.ts is the pattern for a build-time lint that fails Trial Mode if any prescribing/trend copy leaks. lib/safety/redFlags.ts is the adverse-event screen an ethics committee will ask for. docs/cuhk-approach.md is the pitch; the feature makes its one-sentence claim true.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING (8-12 weeks for a shippable v1): adherence event schema {participantId(pseudonymous), exerciseId, prescriptionVersion, startedAt, endedAt, prescribedSets/reps/seconds, completedSets/reps/seconds, source enum, formScore 0-1|null, compensationEvents[], deviceId, appVersion, rulesetHash}; versioned prescription table with clinician id, signature timestamp and lock; Trial Mode feature flag that disables self_guided selection, Coach/Companion nudges, cascade.ts, posture-scan mm/trend output and all curve-change copy; weekly adherence computation with verified and reported figures; CSV/Parquet export + data dictionary + audit log, REDCap-importable; site dashboard for missing-data and device-failure monitoring; raise MIN_PAIRS_FOR_MDC to 10 with CI-adjusted MDC and add ICC(2,1) per the biomech audit; the deterministic safety pre-filter and timestamped safety-answer log from the safety_informatics findings (an ethics committee will require the adverse-event pathway to work). CLINICAL: one PSSE-certified physiotherapist to own the prescription editor and sign off any cue text that remains visible (Tier-3 content must be fixed or removed before any patient sees it in a trial); a supervised-observation validation study (n~20-30, therapist-observed home sessions vs app-logged verified minutes; home-helper phone-ATR test-retest vs clinician scoliometer) - this is the paper that makes the instrument citable. DATA/GOVERNANCE: pseudonymisation at the edge, HK PDPO compliance, CUHK-NTEC CREC ethics submission, data-ownership terms conceded to the study upfront (as cuhk-approach.md recommends), parental consent and child assent in Traditional Chinese and English for any under-18 arm, guardian/clinician gating for minors. PARTNERSHIPS: a CUHK O&T researcher planning the successor to NCT03427970 (or any SOSORT-affiliated PSSE group - the instrument is trial-agnostic), a PSSE clinic for the validation pilot, and a biostatistician to co-author the data dictionary so the export is built to the analysis, not the other way round. Resolve HSBC IP and tag the repo first, per the existing checklist.
proposals.biggest_risk: That "verified" is not verification. The biomech audit rates most single-webcam checks as theatre (hip-height cues, spine rotation, press-down side), and what survives - rep counts, hold timers, side-plank sag - can confirm a body moved in roughly the right way for roughly the right time, not that the prescribed corrective was performed with the prescribed asymmetry or effort. If the validation study shows verified minutes disagree materially with therapist-observed sessions (wrong exercise counted, half-effort holds counted, two-person or off-camera sessions not counted), the instrument collapses to a timestamped diary and the whole premise of the pitch fails in front of the one audience that will check. Mitigation is to define "verified" narrowly and honestly (presence + matched movement pattern + duration, with formScore reported separately and never inflated), publish the agreement statistics before making the claim, keep timer_only and self_report as first-class categories rather than hiding them, and let the trial's own supervised sessions calibrate the home logs. Secondary risks: the app itself becomes a co-intervention (reminders, feedback) that confounds the exercise arm unless Trial Mode is genuinely stripped or randomised as a factor; and NCT03427970 may already be complete, so the timing depends on a successor protocol and a grant cycle the founder does not control.
proposals.evidence_basis: HIGH confidence (verified in repo): persist.ts writes exercises_completed with no denominator, no per-set timestamps, no provenance; tools.ts log_exercise writes chat self-report into the same field; repeatability.ts implements SEM/MDC95/Bland-Altman with a 5-pair gate; parseProgram.ts ingests physio programmes with source_text; docs/cuhk-approach.md frames adherence measurement as the sole differentiator and names NCT03427970 as primary target. HIGH confidence (confirmed audit findings supplied): the adherence and dose findings (evidence/major, evidence/minor) that no prescribed dose or provenance exists; biomech triage of which form checks are plausible vs theatre; safety_informatics findings that the ongoing safety screen is dead code and that no age gate exists. MEDIUM confidence (from the digest, not independently re-verified here): PSSE trial doses (Schreiber 2015/2016 ~30-45 min/day home plus weekly supervised; Yuan 2025 30 min/day, >=5 days/week, 6 months) and the ">=80% per-protocol" adherence convention - consistent with my clinical recollection but no source was fetched in this run. LOW confidence: current recruitment status of NCT03427970 and whether a successor protocol exists - unverified; the plan should not depend on that specific trial. No numeric claims about trial cost or market size are made because none could be sourced.
proposals.time_to_first_value: ~6 weeks to the research-conversation deliverable: adherence event schema, a locked prescription object, a sample pseudonymised export with data dictionary, and a written validation protocol - enough to walk into a CUHK O&T researcher's office with something a statistician can critique. 8-12 weeks to a usable Trial Mode build (ledger, provenance, coaching stripped, export, minors gating). ~3 months after that for the supervised-observation validation pilot that makes "verified adherence" a defensible claim. First trial participant enrolled on the instrument: 6-18 months, governed by ethics approval and the partner's protocol/grant cycle rather than by engineering.

proposals.title: The Watch Window: a clinician-shared observation ledger for HK's observed-but-untreated cohort
proposals.one_liner: Turn Balance from an adult exercise coach into the between-visit monitoring record for every HK schoolchild who screened positive but is only being "observed" — a per-child ledger of helper-measured ATR at the known apex (gated on the child's own repeatability), height velocity and maturity milestones, brace-window status, and PSSE adherence — that the Student Health Service / Special Assessment Centre or orthopaedic clinic receives as a one-page summary at each 6–12-month review, with exercises demoted to an adjunct module inside it.
proposals.why_100x: Mechanism, not adjectives: (1) Cohort size and structure. If ~2.8% of screened students are referred and ~9% of those need treatment, then ~91% of referrals — roughly 2.5% of all screened students, i.e. ~10x the treated group — are placed in watchful waiting. Nobody owns that interval today: the child is seen every 6–12 months, and between visits the family has no instrument, no record, and no way to know whether to come back early. The product that owns the interval owns the cohort. (2) Buyer changes from individual to institution. An exercise coach is sold one adult at a time; an observation ledger is a pathway component that SHS/SAC or a hospital ortho clinic wants for every observed child, because it answers the one question their 6-monthly visit cannot: what happened in the gap. That converts consumer churn into a per-cohort, per-year institutional relationship (and is exactly the "between-visit monitoring, not screening" position docs/cuhk-approach.md already reaches — but never encodes as product). (3) It is the only cohort where the product's exercise content is actually indicated. SOSORT positions PSSE as first-line specifically for small curves in growing patients — which is the definition of the observed cohort. For adults with fixed curves the coach promises pain/function; for observed adolescents it is the guideline-recommended intervention, delivered where it must happen (home) with the adherence provenance the CUHK pitch depends on. (4) The data asset compounds. Longitudinal home ATR at the apex + height velocity + menarche/Risser + adherence + pain, on thousands of observed children, is the input that progression-prediction work (the "three-year conversation" TOCI line in the CUHK doc) does not have. The ledger makes that dataset a by-product of routine care rather than a study you have to fund. (5) It converts the product's honesty into the differentiator. The whole audit says the product cannot claim curve change; a ledger's job is not to claim change but to bring a repeatability-gated reading, a growth spurt flag, and a brace-window prompt to the clinician on time. "Book your SAC visit sooner — your helper readings moved more than your own noise floor and you grew 4 cm in 5 months" is a claim the instrument CAN support, and it is worth more to a family and a clinic than any exercise.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on:
- lib/atr/compute.ts: captureAtr, TRUNK_LEVELS, summarise, atrPairsFrom — the phone-inclinometer ATR and the same-day pair collector; needs the audit fixes (apex-from-report as primary site, sweep mode, orientation confirmation, per-level trend, drop 7° band) but the instrument and the repeatability hook exist.
- lib/pose/repeatability.ts: computeRepeatability / buildMdcTable / describeDetectionLimit — the per-user MDC machinery that makes "changed vs noise" an honest statement; raise MIN_PAIRS_FOR_MDC per the biomech finding and it is the ledger's core gate.
- lib/safety/redFlags.ts three-tier triage + condition-free copy style — the vehicle for the new adolescent items (juvenile onset, painful curve, apex hyperkyphosis, brace-window REVIEW flag).
- Physio handoff PDF + Gemini X-ray REPORT parsing (confirm-per-field) — repurpose the report parser to ingest the SAC/orthopaedic letter (Cobb, apex, convex side, Risser) and the PDF to become the clinic-facing "since last visit" summary.
- selectProgram.ts physio_cleared mode — the mandatory path for minors; the ledger's exercise module is physio_cleared only, capped to Tiers 4–5 when no prescription exists.
- Outcomes module (PSFS, pain days) and the adherence event schema proposed in the evidence findings — the adherence half of the ledger.
- docs/cuhk-approach.md — the institutional route (adherence sub-study with CUHK O&T; between-visit ATR positioning) is already written; this feature is what makes that document a product rather than a pitch.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING (~3 months to a pilotable build, given the audit fixes are prerequisite): (a) ship the ATR fixes (apex-keyed primary site, sweep/max mode, orientation confirmation, zero-offset, 4 s median window, per-level trend, MDC gate at ≥10 pairs with conservative bound); (b) new profile fields: date of birth, sex, menarche status/date, self-measured height log (monthly), Risser/Cobb/apex from clinic letter, brace status and prescribed hours, next scheduled review date; (c) a growth-velocity computation (cm/yr from height log) and a deterministic "bring forward your visit" rule set — ATR change > personal MDC at apex, height velocity above a clinician-set threshold during the immature window, new pain, any red flag — that never emits "stable"; (d) guardian consent + child assent flow, minors default to no LLM chat/no Companion nudges, no scan-derived body numbers; (e) a clinic-facing one-page PDF/CSV per child per interval and a clinic dashboard listing observed children by review-due date and open flags; (f) Traditional Chinese throughout (helper is a parent). CLINICAL: a paediatric spine orthopaedic surgeon and a certified PSSE physiotherapist to set the bring-forward thresholds and sign the exercise tiers permitted for minors; a clinical hazard analysis with the false-reassurance hazard named. DATA: a same-day ATR pair at enrolment plus one at every clinic visit (clinician-measured scoliometer alongside) to establish helper-vs-clinician agreement — this is the validation study and it is small. PARTNERSHIPS: one orthopaedic clinic's observation arm (CUHK O&T via the sub-study framing, or a private paediatric spine clinic) as the pilot; the Department of Health SHS is the eventual counterparty but must not be approached with an unvalidated instrument, and the school cohort must never be recruited through schools without DH. REB: parental consent and child assent in Chinese and English, data-minimisation for minors, named escalation clinician.
proposals.biggest_risk: False reassurance that costs a child the bracing window. ATR–Cobb correlation is only moderate; a curve can progress radiographically while a parent-placed phone at four levels reads flat, and a family holding a ledger of "nothing moved" is exactly the family that skips or defers the SAC visit — the one outcome that makes the product net-harmful. This is compounded by the helper's laterality and level-placement error, and by the institutional risk that a private app sitting alongside the DH pathway is seen as a parallel screener (the comparison the CUHK doc already says you lose). Mitigations must be designed in, not bolted on: the ledger only ever emits "keep your scheduled visit" or "bring it forward"; it never emits reassuring language; the scheduled-review date is a hard field and the product nags toward it; every summary carries "only an X-ray measures your curve"; growth velocity and maturity — not ATR — drive the brace-window prompt. If the team cannot commit to a product that is forbidden to say "stable", it should not build this.
proposals.evidence_basis: Confidence notes (sources not re-fetched this run; figures from memory and from the supplied digest): HIGH — the HK pathway shape: SHS screens students annually from around Primary 5, refers ATR 5–14° to moiré/periodic re-screen and ATR ≥15° or ≥2 moiré lines to radiograph (Luk et al. 2010, Spine; Fong et al. 2015, Spine J) — exact cut-offs to be verified before copy ships, as the digest already requires. MEDIUM — the ~2.8% referral / ~9% needing treatment figures are as given in the brief; the derived "observed ≈ 10x treated" follows arithmetically and is the load-bearing claim; the absolute cohort size (tens of thousands of HK children under observation at any time) is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a verified number. HIGH — SOSORT 2016 guidelines (Negrini et al. 2018) recommend PSSE for small curves in growing patients and bracing from roughly 20–25° with growth remaining; BrAIST (Weinstein et al. 2013, NEJM) established bracing efficacy, which is why the window matters. MEDIUM — peak height velocity / growth spurt and Risser/menarche as progression predictors are standard (Lonstein & Carlson 1984; Sanders et al.), but I have not verified specific velocity thresholds and the product should take them from its clinical advisors. MEDIUM — helper-measured scoliometer agreement with clinicians is not established (the digest's biomech finding); the enrolment-visit pairing is the proposed fix and is unproven. HIGH (from repo) — docs/cuhk-approach.md already positions ATR as between-visit monitoring and names CUHK NCT03427970/NCT03904914; repeatability and pair-collection code exists in lib/pose/repeatability.ts and lib/atr/compute.ts.
proposals.time_to_first_value: First value to a family: at the second same-day ATR pair (enrolment + first repeat), i.e. within the first clinic interval — the child gets a personal noise floor and a "bring this to your visit" summary instead of nothing. First value to a clinic: the first review cycle after pilot start (~6 months), when the clinician receives between-visit summaries for an observation-arm caseload. Build time: ~3 months of engineering after the prerequisite audit fixes (ATR, minors gate, library convention) plus REB approval running in parallel (~3–6 months in HK); realistic first pilot data at 9–12 months, and the institutional (DH/SHS) conversation only after a clinic pilot has shown helper-vs-clinician agreement.

proposals.title: Physio-Recorded Home Programme with a Weekly Verified Review Loop
proposals.one_liner: In the clinic, the physio records each prescribed exercise on the patient's own body (30-second clip plus their spoken cue, in Cantonese or English); at home the app replays the physio's voice and clip, timestamps and form-verifies each set against that reference, and every week the physio gets a three-minute review screen of flagged clips and verified adherence against the dose they set. Balance stops being an algorithmic coach with its own library and becomes the rail that carries a named clinician's prescription into the patient's living room and carries proof back.
proposals.why_100x: Three mechanisms, none of them adjectives. (1) Retention: the thing that keeps an adolescent or adult doing home exercise at week 26 is not a novel cascade chart or a rib-hump photo, it is accountability to a real person who will look. Today nobody looks between appointments; the physio sees a paper sheet and a shrug. When the patient knows Ms Wong reviews Sunday night, and the cue they hear is Ms Wong's own voice saying the exact phrase she used in the room, the exercise stays anchored to a relationship rather than to a chatbot persona. Self-guided programmes decay in weeks; supervised-and-fed-back ones are the only home-exercise model with a plausible 6-month adherence story (confidence: medium, general home-exercise-adherence literature, not verified against a specific citation in this run). (2) Distribution and 'who must have it': the buyer flips from one patient at a time to one clinic at a time. A Schroth/SEAS-trained physio carries tens to hundreds of active scoliosis patients; enrolling a patient becomes part of the appointment, not a download decision. The clinic must have it because it is the only way their prescription reaches the home intact and the only way they can see whether it was done. (3) Liability and content: every major finding in the audit (backwards waist fold, invented cascades, unsourced frog, folk-wisdom absolute bans, Schroth trademark exposure) exists because the product authors clinical content. With the physio recording the cue on the patient's own body, side-keyed cue generation, the concave/convex convention, the curve-pattern taxonomy and the contraindication engine all move from 'things Balance must get right for every phenotype' to 'things the certified clinician already got right for this one person'. The library becomes optional demo content. This also makes the CUHK data claim true for the first time: adherence becomes completed verified minutes divided by a dose the physio actually prescribed, with provenance, which is exactly what docs/cuhk-approach.md says the product should be, an instrument that measures whether the exercise happened.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: physio_cleared mode in lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts already treats the physio programme as authoritative; the parse-program LLM and contraindication regex in lib/exercises/contraindications.ts become a structured (side, load, hold) importer for the physio's typed notes rather than the safety gate. lib/exercises/formCheck/sidePlank, hipBridge and lunge rep-counting are the parts the biomech audit calls plausible; they survive as set/rep/hold verification against the physio's clip, while the theatre cues (L/R hip drop, spine rotation) are dropped. lib/session/persist.ts exercises_completed and lib/agents/context.ts AdherenceSnapshot are the seed of the adherence-event schema (add prescribedDose, source: form_check_verified|timer_only|self_report, formScore, clipRef). app/api/agents/liaison/route.ts plus the appointments table and lib/messaging/deliver.ts already run a 24h-before-appointment handoff; that becomes the weekly clinician digest. app/care-team/page.tsx is a ready skeleton for the clinician review dashboard (rename, add role auth). lib/tts.ts is replaced by playback of the physio's recorded audio. The Telegram Companion keeps its nudge plumbing but its message becomes 'your physio reviewed your week' instead of an LLM-invented micro-movement. The handoff PDF becomes the patient-facing summary of what the physio saw.
proposals.what_it_needs: Engineering: clinician role and multi-tenant model (physio -> patients) with invite codes; an in-clinic capture flow on the physio's phone (per exercise: 20-40 s video, 10 s audio cue, sets/reps/hold, side, dose per week; target under 90 s per exercise); secure media storage with expiry and HK PDPO-compliant retention; home playback screen that plays the physio's voice and clip beside the patient's camera; form verification reduced to rep/hold counting and side-plank sag against the clinic reference; weekly review screen (verified minutes vs prescribed, flagged clips, pain and PSFS trend, one-tap 'seen, keep going' / 'change this' that pushes a re-recorded cue); adherence event schema with provenance and CSV export. Clinical: two or three Schroth/SEAS-certified physios as design partners who own the content; the existing self-guided library relabelled as conditioning demo content and disabled for anyone under 18. Data: consent flows for video of minors (guardian consent plus adolescent assent in Traditional Chinese and English), a stated retention window, and a red-flag escalation path that notifies the named physio. Partnerships: one HK private scoliosis physio clinic for a 10-patient pilot; CUHK as the study partner who wants the verified-adherence denominator.
proposals.biggest_risk: The physio is the bottleneck and the product dies if they do not record and review. If capture adds more than a couple of minutes to a 30-minute appointment, or the Sunday review is unpaid work that is not billable as telehealth, physios will skip recording after the second patient, the patient's home screen is empty, and Balance is back to serving its own unsourced library. Secondary but real: storing video of adolescents' backs creates a safeguarding and privacy exposure that a school-screening cohort pilot will be judged on before any clinical merit is considered. Mitigations to design in from day one: capture in under 90 s per exercise with the phone the physio already holds; review screen answerable in under three minutes with a default 'nothing to change'; pilot with adults first; a hard rule that no minor's video leaves the device without guardian consent, and a fallback text-plus-audio prescription when video consent is refused.
proposals.evidence_basis: Built on the confirmed audit findings rather than new claims: the product's own physio_cleared mode is already treated as authoritative; every content-level clinical error found (waist fold, frog, cascades, absolute bans, Schroth naming) is an artefact of Balance authoring cues itself; docs/cuhk-approach.md concludes the honest role is measuring whether prescribed exercise happened; the Yuan et al. 2025 digital-PSSE trial (as summarised in the digest) tested remote supervision of physiotherapist-prescribed PSSE, not an app in place of a physio, so a supervised-prescription rail is the only shape of Balance that could ever be a credible comparator. The claim that a named reviewer and personalised cues improve home-exercise adherence is consistent with the general home-exercise-adherence literature but I did not verify a specific source in this run: treat that as medium confidence. No numbers, DOIs or effect sizes are asserted here beyond those already in the digest.
proposals.time_to_first_value: Six to eight weeks to a working pilot: clinician role, capture flow, home playback with timer-only verification, and a weekly review screen with verified-minutes-vs-dose. The patient hears their own physio's voice on day one of the pilot; the physio sees their first verified adherence week within seven days. Form verification against the clinic reference clip and the adolescent consent flow follow in the next quarter, after the adult pilot proves physios will actually record and review.

proposals.title: The Signed Prescription Loop: physio-authored programme in, verified-dose ledger out
proposals.one_liner: Invert the product: the physiotherapist authors and signs the programme (exercises, sides, dose, method) in a 5-minute clinician screen; Balance's only job between visits is to deliver exactly that prescription, verify with the webcam/timer that it was done, and hand the clinician a weekly one-page ledger of verified minutes, form breaks, pain and ATR-at-apex against the dose they set.
proposals.why_100x: Three multiplications, not adjectives. (1) Who must have it changes: today the buyer is a patient hunting for exercises; after this the buyer is the scoliosis physio, and each physio carries 50-200 active patients, so one clinician conversion is worth ~100 patient conversions and the acquisition channel becomes referral-at-the-appointment ('install this before you leave, I have already put your programme in'). A physio insists on it because it solves THEIR unsolved problem: PSSE only works at 30-45 min/day for months (Schreiber 2015/16; Yuan 2025 dose) and they currently have zero visibility of whether that happens; today's paper diary is exactly what docs/cuhk-approach.md criticises. (2) What the product is changes: every confirmed audit finding that is dangerous (inverted waist-fold cue, fold-left founder leakage, 'absolute' Fishman side-plank rule, invented cascade chains, X-ray-photo laterality flips, self-report convexity guessing, unsourced frog exercise) shares one root cause - the algorithm is the prescriber. Move authority to a named licensed clinician and those become non-issues: sides come from the physio's typed 'right' not from 'which way does your back bulge'; contraindications become 'not in your prescription' rather than pseudo-absolute bans; the LLM is demoted to adherence/reflection only, which is the one job the evidence review says it may keep. The library shrinks to a rendering/coaching layer for whatever the clinician signs. Regulatory and ethics exposure for the HK adolescent cohort collapses for the same reason: a supervised, clinician-prescribed adjunct is a fundamentally different object from an autonomous exercise recommender for minors. (3) What the data are worth changes: with a stored prescription snapshot there is finally a denominator, so adherence = verified minutes / prescribed minutes per week - the trial-grade variable every PSSE RCT lacks. That is what makes CUHK (or any Schroth/SEAS clinic) want to run a study on top of it, and a product that is the adherence instrument inside other people's trials is the honest positioning the codebase's own strategy doc already reached. Self-guided mode survives only as a stripped Tier 4-5 symmetric mobility/breathing path (SOSORT-permissive, no side cues) while the patient waits for a clinician.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: Roughly 70% of the substrate is already in the repo, pointed the wrong way. lib/prompts/parseProgram.ts + app/api/parse-program/route.ts already parse informal physio shorthand into structured exercises with source_text, asymmetric_cues, reps/sets/duration and library_match_id - this becomes the clinician's authoring assistant (they paste, review, sign) instead of a patient-side paste box. selectProgram.ts physio_cleared mode already treats the pasted programme as authoritative; it needs to become the ONLY mode that unlocks side-keyed cues. lib/exercises/formCheck/{birdDog,hipBridge,lunge,sidePlank,tStretch}.ts already produce rep counts, hold timers and timestamped compensation events; only the plausible checks (side-plank sag/pike/head, hip-bridge and lunge rep counting, T-stretch back-knee, hold timers) are used for 'verified', and the L/R pelvic checks the biomech audit calls theatre are excluded from the ledger. lib/session/persist.ts exercises_completed and lib/agents/tools.ts log_exercise already write completion rows - they need the source flag (form_check_verified | timer_only | chat_self_report) and a prescription snapshot id. app/api/agents/liaison/* already builds a handoff 24h pre-appointment with questions_for_physio - it becomes a weekly clinician digest with a fixed, non-LLM numeric header (verified minutes vs prescribed, days adherent, form-break count, pain, PSFS, ATR at physio-nominated apex level) and LLM prose only below the line. app/care-team/page.tsx is a ready skeleton for the clinician view. lib/atr/compute.ts supplies the between-visit ATR trend the moment the physio enters the apex level and per-user MDC gating (lib/pose/repeatability.ts) exists. lib/outcomes/compute.ts PSFS + side-bridge/Sorensen provide the function/endurance columns. redFlags.ts emergency gating and the Telegram flag_safety path stay, now also notifying the named clinician.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING (8-12 weeks to a pilotable build): a clinician account type and patient-link (invite code at the appointment); a prescription authoring screen: paste-or-pick from library, per-exercise side enum (left/right/both) and dose (sets/reps/seconds, days/week, minutes/day) with parse-program pre-filling and mandatory clinician confirmation; a signed, versioned prescription snapshot table; the adherence-event schema from the evidence audit (exerciseId, startedAt/endedAt, prescribed vs completed, source, formScore, compensationEvents, deviceId); weekly verified/reported adherence computation; a one-page clinician digest (web + PDF + optional Telegram/WhatsApp link) with a CSV export per patient; retire self_guided asymmetric cues, cascade.ts and inferStiffHipFlexorSide; add spinal_fusion/brace/pregnancy/osteoporosis intake so the physio sees the population profile. CLINICAL: one Schroth- or SEAS-certified physio as design partner who signs off the authoring vocabulary and the 'verified' definition, and who accepts that only rep/hold/timer signals count as verified in v1; fix the confirmed library errors (waist fold, child's-pose rationale, side-plank tier) before any clinician sees the library. DATA: 5-10 same-day ATR pairs per patient for MDC; a Bland-Altman of webcam rep counts vs a human observer on ~20 sessions to justify the word 'verified'. PARTNERSHIPS: 1-2 scoliosis physio clinics in HK for a 10-20 patient feasibility pilot with adherence/pain/PSFS endpoints; CUHK as the trial-instrument route later, not first. BUSINESS: pricing per clinician seat, not per patient.
proposals.biggest_risk: That 'verified' is theatre and the physio discovers it. If the webcam rep/hold counts are noisy (patient off-frame, side-view occlusion, MediaPipe L/R swaps), the ledger over- or under-reports dose and a clinician who catches one wrong number never opens the digest again - and a wrong 'verified' figure is WORSE than a paper diary because it carries false objectivity into a chart or a trial dataset. Second-order version of the same risk: clinicians will not spend 5 minutes authoring per patient unless the parse-program pre-fill is near-perfect, and a half-adopted loop leaves patients back in self-guided mode with the algorithm as prescriber - the exact state this feature exists to abolish. Mitigations: ship 'verified' only for the plausible single-camera signals, show n and confidence on every ledger number, run the observer-agreement study before using the word, and make the clinician's authoring flow a review-and-sign of the parse rather than data entry. A third, structural risk: a clinician-facing prescription-and-monitoring tool edges toward software-as-a-medical-device classification in HK/UK/EU; keeping all clinical decisions with the human and the app as a delivery/record layer is the defensible line, but this needs a regulatory opinion before a paid launch.
proposals.evidence_basis: HIGH confidence (verified against the digest and repo): every dangerous audit finding traces to algorithmic prescription; parse-program, physio_cleared mode, form-check engines, Liaison and exercises_completed exist and can be repointed; no prescribed-dose denominator exists today; exerciseContraindicated() excludes nothing; docs/cuhk-approach.md already frames the product as 'the instrument that measures whether the exercise happened'. MEDIUM confidence (from clinical knowledge, not re-verified online in this run): Yuan et al. 2025 showed remotely physio-supervised digital PSSE outperformed in-person + unsupervised home PSSE by about 4 degrees Cobb between groups at 30 min/day, 5+ days/week for 6 months - i.e. the winning ingredient was clinician-prescribed content plus digital supervision/adherence, which is precisely this feature and precisely not an autonomous app; Schreiber 2015/2016 Schroth RCTs used 30-45 min/day home practice; SOSORT 2016 positions PSSE as adjunctive to bracing in growing patients and permissive on general activity; adherence in PSSE trials is typically defined as proportion of prescribed dose with ~80% per-protocol thresholds. LOW confidence / assumption: the 50-200 active patients per scoliosis physio figure and the willingness of HK clinics to pay per seat are estimates from clinical practice patterns, not measured; the observer-agreement study for webcam rep counting has not been done and its result is unknown.
proposals.time_to_first_value: First clinician value (one physio sees a real patient's weekly verified-vs-prescribed ledger and ATR at their nominated apex) in 8-12 weeks: weeks 1-3 fix the confirmed library/side errors and retire self-guided asymmetric cues, cascade and hip-flexor inference; weeks 3-7 clinician account, prescription authoring/sign-off over the existing parse-program, adherence-event schema and prescription snapshots; weeks 7-10 weekly digest with fixed numeric header plus CSV export, and the 20-session observer-agreement check on rep counting; weeks 10-12 pilot with one design-partner clinic and 10-20 patients. Trial-instrument value (CUHK-style adherence sub-study) realistically 6-9 months, after the pilot yields per-user ATR MDCs and verified-count agreement data.

proposals.title: The Observation Ledger: own the six-month gap between school-screening visits
proposals.one_liner: Turn Balance from an adult exercise coach into the between-visit monitoring record for the HK Student Health Service's "observed, not treated" adolescents — a parent-held, clinician-readable ledger of apex ATR (MDC-gated), growth velocity, maturity and pain that fills the interval nobody in the pathway currently owns, with exercise demoted to an optional symmetric adjunct.
proposals.why_100x: The arithmetic of the HK pathway is the argument. Nearly every student is screened; ~2.8% are referred; only ~9% of those need treatment. That leaves ~91% of referrals — the largest scoliosis cohort in the territory, on the order of tens of thousands of children at any time (order-of-magnitude estimate from the given rates and HK school population; confidence medium) — in an observation arm: told the curve is small, come back in 6–12 months for re-screen/moiré/clinic. Between those visits there is no instrument, no record, no owner. Yet that interval is precisely where progression happens, because it coincides with peak height velocity, and it is where the pathway's real failure lives: a child re-screened after a growth spurt has already progressed, or a frightened parent has bought a private X-ray the SHS was deliberately avoiding. Three mechanisms multiply value: (1) POPULATION, not niche — the product stops competing with physiotherapists for adults who already have a programme and instead serves a state-created cohort that arrives pre-identified, pre-motivated (a letter from the SHS) and with a parent as the helper the ATR protocol already requires; (2) WHO MUST HAVE IT changes from "patient who wants exercises" to "screening programme and orthopaedic clinic that cannot see the child for six months" — the ledger (apex ATR trend with per-child repeatability, monthly height, menarche/growth-spurt stamps, pain) is the only between-visit data a clinician can act on, and the handoff PDF becomes the artefact that decides whether a child is brought forward, which makes the clinic the distribution channel rather than a sales target; (3) DATA — longitudinal ATR + growth velocity + adherence + pain across an observed cohort is exactly the input a progression-prediction line (the CUHK TOCI work named in docs/cuhk-approach.md) lacks, so the product's long-term asset is the dataset, not the exercise library. The current product's most defensible components (ATR, MDC machinery, red-flag screen, handoff PDF) are all monitoring components; the components the audit found weakest (asymmetric cues, cascades, posture scan) are exercise components. The 100x move is to build the product around what is defensible and for the cohort where it is scarce.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: lib/atr/compute.ts (phone inclinometer, four levels, stability gates, 5° HK carry-forward threshold already cited in code) and atrPairsFrom() feeding lib/pose/repeatability.ts (SEM/MDC95) — the core of a per-child trend engine already exists, it only needs the audit fixes (sign/orientation confirmation, sweep-to-maximum mode, zero-offset, 4 s median window, gamma reframed as bend-depth guide, per-level trending, and the recommended jurisdiction config with HK bands 5–14 → SHS/moiré follow-up, ≥15 → SHS radiograph referral). lib/safety/redFlags.ts (9 rules, tiered, condition-free copy; atypical left-thoracic <18 rule is already scoliosis-specific and merely unreachable because ageYears is never written). lib/outcomes/compute.ts (PSFS, good-days, MDC gating) for pain/function. The physio handoff PDF generator as the seed of a clinician summary. lib/messaging + Telegram companion as the reminder channel — repointed at the parent/helper, not the child. Onboarding X-ray REPORT parsing (report text path, not image) for baseline Cobb/apex when a clinic radiograph exists. lib/cn.ts as a starting point for Traditional Chinese. docs/cuhk-approach.md already reaches the between-visit-monitoring framing; this feature encodes it as the product.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING (8–12 weeks to pilot): ATR audit fixes above; jurisdiction threshold config with HK copy; date-of-birth, sex, height log (monthly, with derived growth velocity), menarche status, self-reported growth spurt, Risser/Cobb from report if known; a "Not sure" everywhere; guardian consent + adolescent assent records; minor gate that disables self-guided asymmetric exercise, free-text LLM chat, posture-scan numbers and any "stable/improving" language for <18; ledger export (per-child one-page clinician summary + CSV); Traditional Chinese first-class. CLINICAL: a paediatric spine clinician to sign the copy and the escalation rules (growth velocity above threshold or ATR change beyond per-child MDC → "bring your SHS/clinic visit forward"; Cobb ≥20–25° + immature → "ask about bracing", exercise labelled adjunctive); helper-ATR repeatability study against clinic scoliometer/Scolioscan (~50 pairs) to replace the "MDC unknown" placeholder — expect 3–4°. DATA/GOVERNANCE: data-minimisation for minors, PDPO-compliant storage in HK, adverse-event pathway naming a clinician, REB submission (parental consent, child assent, false-reassurance hazard plan). PARTNERSHIPS: the only ones that matter — a CUHK/HKU orthopaedic scoliosis clinic observation arm as pilot site (framed as an observational sub-study, no ethics amendment), then Department of Health Student Health Service as the eventual distribution channel; do not recruit via schools without DH. The exercise library becomes a symmetric mobility/breathing adjunct and a physio_cleared channel only.
proposals.biggest_risk: False reassurance at population scale. ATR correlates only moderately with Cobb, helper-placed phone readings will have an MDC of several degrees, and a 5–10° Cobb progression during a growth spurt can sit entirely inside that noise. If a parent reads "no change" and defers or skips the SHS re-screen, the product has converted the pathway's one safety net into a hazard — for tens of thousands of children, with the Department of Health's name adjacent to it. This is exactly the danger the team's own strategy doc identifies (telling a growing adolescent the curve is stable). The design must make it structurally impossible: never emit "stable"; only "no change larger than your measurement noise (± X°) — this cannot detect small progression"; every summary ends with the next scheduled SHS/clinic date; growth-velocity triggers force an earlier-visit prompt independently of ATR; and the product must never be positioned as an alternative to re-screening. Secondary risks: DH is slow and medico-legally cautious, so the population channel may take years while a clinic pilot is the only near-term reality; and a phone next to Scolioscan invites a comparison the phone loses unless framed strictly as between-visit trend.
proposals.evidence_basis: HK SHS funnel rates (≈all screened, ~2.8% referred, ~9% of referrals treated) taken from the brief; cohort-size estimate derived from them, confidence medium. HK pathway details (ATR 5–14° → moiré/periodic re-screen; radiograph at ATR ≥15° or ≥2 moiré lines) from recollection of the Luk et al. 2010 / Fong et al. 2015 programme descriptions cited in the audit — confidence medium, must be verified against the papers before any copy ships. Progression risk concentrating around peak height velocity in immature AIS and bracing indicated at roughly Cobb 20–25° with growth remaining (SOSORT 2016 framing) — confidence high as general clinical knowledge, exact thresholds to be cited from the guideline. Moderate ATR–Cobb correlation and clinician scoliometer ICC 0.94–0.99 under clinician placement (Bunnell; validation studies named in code comments) — confidence high; helper-at-home repeatability is UNKNOWN, as the audit states. CUHK lines of work (NCT03427970 exercise trial, NCT03135665 ultrasound screening, NCT03904914 TOCI progression prediction) from docs/cuhk-approach.md; registration status unverified today. No source found for any existing product owning the observed cohort in HK — absence claimed from the brief's own framing, confidence low-medium. I did not run web searches in this pass; nothing above cites a DOI or number not present in the brief or repo.
proposals.time_to_first_value: 8–12 weeks to a clinic-pilot-ready ledger (ATR fixes, HK thresholds, DOB/consent/growth capture, minor gate, clinician summary, Traditional Chinese) for a single observation-arm sub-study of ~30–50 families; first clinically useful output — a per-child ATR repeatability estimate and growth-velocity flag — at the second visit, i.e. ~3–6 months after enrolment; population-scale value via DH/SHS is a 12–24 month partnership horizon and should not be assumed in planning.

proposals.title: Verified-Dose Adherence Instrument (trial-grade prescription-vs-delivery ledger with statistician export)
proposals.one_liner: Turn Balance from a coach that guesses what you should do into the instrument that proves what you actually did: a locked, physio-authored prescription snapshot plus a per-set, camera-verified adherence ledger (exercise, timestamps, prescribed vs completed dose, form score, provenance) exported as a pre-specified CSV/data dictionary that a CUHK statistician can drop straight into a per-protocol analysis.
proposals.why_100x: Mechanism, not adjectives: today every home PSSE trial (Schreiber 2015/2016, Yuan 2025, CUHK NCT03427970) has an un-measurable independent variable. Adherence is diary or recall, both known to overstate, so a null result cannot be distinguished from non-delivery and a positive result cannot be dose-response analysed. That is a methodological hole in the primary interpretation of a trial costing seven figures, and no vendor sells a fix. An instrument that emits objective per-set delivery data (verified minutes / prescribed minutes, weekly, with form quality and provenance) is not 'an app patients might like' — it is a protocol-level measurement device that gets named in the Methods section, drives the per-protocol and dose-response analyses, and is therefore something the PI must have in the design rather than something they can tolerate. The value multiplication comes from three switches: (1) the customer changes from an individual patient (HK$0–100/month, unvalidated content, severe liability) to a research group and, downstream, every PSSE trial and bracing+PSSE trial globally — a small number of high-value, low-churn, ethics-gated customers; (2) the product's clinical content becomes irrelevant to its value — the physio prescribes, Balance measures — which retires every critical finding in the audit (backwards waist-fold cue, Fishman side-plank 'contraindication', invented cascades, Cobb-from-photo) in one move because self-guided prescription stops being load-bearing; (3) it produces the one dataset nobody has — patient-years of verified dose against Cobb/ATR/SRS-22r outcomes — which is the only credible road to the TOCI/progression-prediction conversation the team's own docs call the three-year prize. Concretely: a physio enters or pastes the prescription (already parsed by physio_programs) with minutesPerDay and daysPerWeek; the prescription is snapshotted with a version id; each set produces an immutable adherence_event {exerciseId, startedAt, endedAt, prescribedSets/reps/seconds, completedSets/reps/seconds, source: form_check_verified | timer_only | chat_self_report | manual, formScore 0–1 or null, compensationEvents[], deviceId, prescriptionVersion}; weekly adherence = verified minutes / prescribed minutes, reported alongside a separate 'reported' figure; export is a versioned CSV + data dictionary + REDCap-compatible id mapping, with the participant identified only by study code.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: Roughly 70% of the plumbing exists but is not wired for evidence: lib/exercises/formCheck/* already emits rep_completed, hold_progress, compensation(id, severity), form_excellent events per frame — these are the raw material for per-set formScore and compensationEvents but are currently discarded except as a SessionSummary {exerciseId, setsCompleted, details[{repsCompleted, holdSeconds}]} (components/exercise/ExerciseCoach.tsx:68). lib/session/persist.ts writes that summary to sessions.exercises_completed (jsonb) — the ledger replaces this with a typed adherence_events table. lib/agents/tools.ts toolLogExercise already writes chat self-reports into the SAME array with no provenance flag — the fix is a one-line source='chat_self_report'. supabase/schema.sql already has physio_programs (raw_source, parsed_exercises) as the prescription object and sessions/appointments/liaison_documents for the clinician loop; lib/agents/context.ts AdherenceSnapshot (sessionsLast7Days etc.) is the numerator-only metric to be replaced with a denominator-aware one. lib/pose/repeatability.ts and lib/outcomes/compute.ts (PSFS, side-bridge, Sorensen, MDC machinery) supply secondary outcomes and the repeatability method a reviewer will ask for. lib/atr/compute.ts atrPairsFrom() is the between-visit ATR trend. selectProgram.ts physio_cleared mode is already the 'prescription is authoritative' path — it becomes the only path in study mode. docs/cuhk-approach.md already articulates exactly this framing ('a trial that can finally tell whether the exercise was actually done'); the code simply does not deliver it yet. The Liaison agent and handoff PDF become the weekly clinician review surface.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING (4–8 weeks, one strong full-stack dev): adherence_events table + prescription_snapshots table with append-only semantics and RLS; per-set persistence of formCheck events with timestamps and a formScore aggregate; provenance enum on every event and hard separation of 'verified' vs 'reported' adherence; prescription fields minutesPerDay/daysPerWeek on physio_programs and a versioned snapshot per week; a 'study mode' flag that disables self_guided selection, LLM-invented cues, posture-scan mm numbers and cascade copy, and locks the exercise list to the prescription; CSV/data-dictionary export keyed by study code with no PII (agents already redact the name — extend to export); an audit log; offline-tolerant event queue. Formal MDC/ICC reporting for the form-check verification itself (a small validation: verified-rep count vs blinded video review on ~30 sessions), because the instrument's own measurement properties will be asked for. CLINICAL: a physio (ideally the trial's own) to author the prescription templates and sign off the dose presets; a clinician-reviewed decision that the form-check output is 'delivery evidence', not 'quality judgement'; the audit-mandated fixes that would embarrass the product in a protocol review — remove/downgrade the Fishman side-plank contraindication, fix or drop sitting_waist_fold, strip 'Schroth' and 'progression/drift' language, add fusion/brace/age intake — because a PI will read the whole product before adopting one module. DATA/GOVERNANCE: HK PDPO-compliant data-processing agreement, data stored in a jurisdiction CUHK's REB accepts, pre-specified data dictionary and analysis-ready schema, a statement that CUHK owns study data (docs/cuhk-approach.md already concedes this), device/browser compatibility matrix for the school-aged cohort's phones, Traditional Chinese UI for participants. PARTNERSHIPS: one investigator on the exercise trial line (not the chair) willing to run an observational adherence sub-study or design the instrument into a successor protocol; an ethics amendment or new submission (expect 3–6 months); resolve the HSBC IP question and tag the repo first, as the docs say.
proposals.biggest_risk: That the 'verified' bit is not actually verifiable. The audit's biomech finding is blunt: from a single webcam, rep counting for hip bridge and lunge, side-plank sag/pike, and T-stretch knee angle are plausible; bird-dog hip drop, spine rotation, hip-bridge L/R unevenness and pelvic cues are 'theatre', dominated by perspective and MediaPipe hip-landmark noise. If the export claims form-verified adherence and a blinded video review or a sceptical statistician shows the rep counter over-counts, under-counts, or cannot tell a full rep from a half-hearted one, the instrument is worse than a diary — it is a diary with false precision, and the team loses the one relationship it needs. Second-order version of the same risk: participants game it (camera on, body half out of frame, timer running), so 'timer_only' minutes masquerade as delivery. Mitigations are mandatory, not optional: (a) ship only presence-and-rep-count-level verification with published sensitivity/specificity from a small blinded validation, and label everything else 'reported'; (b) store short landmark traces (not video) so events are re-auditable; (c) report three tiers separately — camera-verified, timer-only, self-reported — and let the statistician choose. A distinct, lesser risk: CUHK's exercise trial (NCT03427970) may be closed to recruitment, so the realistic first customer is a successor protocol or an observational sub-study — a 6–18 month sales cycle, during which a solo founder has no revenue. Note: I could not verify current trial status or Yuan 2025 dose details against a live source in this run (tooling not exercised); trial-status and dose claims are therefore confidence 'medium' and must be checked before any pitch.
proposals.evidence_basis: HIGH confidence (verified in code this run): formCheck event stream exists but is discarded beyond sets/reps/hold (formCheck/types.ts; ExerciseCoach.tsx SessionSummary); chat self-reports and camera sessions share sessions.exercises_completed with no provenance (lib/agents/tools.ts toolLogExercise; lib/session/persist.ts); AdherenceSnapshot has no denominator (lib/agents/context.ts:112); physio_programs and liaison_documents tables exist (supabase/schema.sql); docs/cuhk-approach.md already frames the adherence-instrument pitch and names NCT03427970 as the primary target. HIGH confidence (methodological, standard trial practice): per-protocol analyses require adherence as proportion of prescribed dose with a pre-specified threshold, commonly around 80%; self-reported home-exercise adherence is known to overstate relative to objective measures. MEDIUM confidence (from the digest and memory, not re-verified against sources this run): PSSE trials with Cobb effects used stated doses in the 30–45 min/day, 5–7 d/wk range for ~6 months (Schreiber 2015/2016; Yuan et al. 2025), and Yuan's −4.23° figure is a between-group difference in a trial of digital supervision, not an app-vs-nothing effect; single-webcam pelvic L/R cues are unreliable while rep counting and collinear-landmark sag checks are plausible (biomech audit). LOW confidence: current recruitment status of NCT03427970 and whether a successor protocol exists — must be checked on clinicaltrials.gov before approach. No citations, DOIs or numbers have been invented; where a number is stated it is either from the codebase or from the confirmed audit digest.
proposals.time_to_first_value: Internal first value in ~2 weeks: provenance flag on adherence events, prescription dose fields, and a verified-vs-reported weekly adherence figure visible in the handoff PDF for the founder's own physio. Pitch-ready instrument in 6–8 weeks: adherence_events table, study mode, CSV + data dictionary export, and a 20–30 session blinded validation of the rep counter to quote. First external value (an investigator agreeing to an observational adherence sub-study or naming the instrument in a successor protocol draft) realistically 3–6 months after that, gated by ethics; first analysable trial data 12–18 months. The founder's own docs sequence the IP/HSBC clean-up before any meeting; that is on the critical path and is not engineering time.

proposals.title: Verified Dose: a validated home dosimeter for prescribed scoliosis exercise
proposals.one_liner: Turn the existing webcam form-check and session store into a single defensible measurement — minutes of prescribed exercise actually performed, in position, per exercise, per day, with a published reliability study against direct observation — and stop claiming anything about the curve at all.
proposals.why_100x: Every measurement the product currently surfaces (posture mm, cascade 'drift', ATR bands, side-bridge ratio) fails the audit for the same reason: it is trying to measure the SPINE from a phone or webcam, which cannot be done validly at home. The one quantity a webcam CAN measure validly at home is the one that matters most to everyone paying for scoliosis exercise and that nobody currently has: whether the prescribed dose was delivered. PSSE trials (Schreiber 2015/2016, Yuan 2025) prescribe 30–45 min/day for 6 months and measure adherence by paper diary or recall — so a null result cannot distinguish 'exercise does not work' from 'nobody did it'. Schroth/SEAS clinics bill for home programmes they cannot see. Bracing follow-up asks parents whether the child exercised. Insurers and the HK Student Health Service have no denominator for 'adherent'. A device that reports, per patient, 'prescribed 210 min/week, camera-verified 143 min in-position, 31 min self-reported unverified, form-break rate 12%' with a known ICC and limits of agreement against video-rated observation is a trial instrument and a clinical monitoring tool, not a consumer coach. That changes the buyer from 'a patient who might download it' to 'a trial PI or clinic that MUST have it to interpret their own intervention' — the product becomes the adherence dosimeter that sits underneath every other group's PSSE, which is exactly the positioning docs/cuhk-approach.md already reached ('the instrument that measures whether the exercise happened') but the code and copy do not yet implement.
