Mechanism of multiplication: (1) it is the only claim the audit leaves standing, so it can be made without a physio-certification or radiographic evidence base; (2) it is method-agnostic — Schroth, SEAS, BSPTS, generic physio programme, in-brace or out-of-brace — so the addressable population is every home-exercise prescription rather than the founder's own curve pattern; (3) validity is achievable at home because the measured quantity (time in a recognisable body configuration, rep/hold counts, presence, timestamp) is in the image plane and coarse — exactly the items the biomech audit triaged as PLAUSIBLE (rep counting, hold timers, side-plank line), not the L/R pelvic items it triaged as THEATRE; (4) the data product (per-patient CSV: exerciseId, startedAt, endedAt, prescribed vs completed, source=form_check_verified|timer_only|chat_self_report, formBreakEvents) is what a trial statistician can pre-register against, and that is worth a hundred consumer downloads.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: lib/exercises/formCheck/{hipBridge,lunge,sidePlank,birdDog,tStretch}.ts already implement rep detection (hip-y oscillation, hip descent) and hold timers with 'pauses if out of position >0.5s' (sidePlank) — the time-in-position primitive is there; types.ts has mode 'reps'|'hold' and holdSeconds. lib/session/persist.ts writes exercises_completed (currently only {exerciseId, setsCompleted}); lib/agents/context.ts AdherenceSnapshot and lib/agents/tools.ts log_exercise (chat self-report, source 'real') are the ingestion points that need a provenance flag. lib/pose/repeatability.ts (SEM/MDC95, atrPairsFrom pattern) is the machinery to compute per-user and pooled reliability of the verified-minutes measure. physio_cleared mode in lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts already treats the pasted physio programme as authoritative — that programme becomes the prescription snapshot / denominator. The handoff PDF is the delivery vehicle for the per-patient report. docs/cuhk-approach.md already contains the pitch and identifies NCT exercise trials as the target.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING: (a) prescription snapshot as first-class data — minutesPerDay, daysPerWeek, per-exercise sets/reps/hold — stored weekly (physio-entered or preset) so adherence has a denominator; (b) adherence event schema {exerciseId, startedAt, endedAt, prescribed, completed, source: form_check_verified|timer_only|chat_self_report|manual, inPositionSeconds, formBreakEvents[], cameraPlacementCheck, deviceId}, appended per set, replacing the flat exercises_completed array; log_exercise writes source=chat_self_report and is excluded from 'verified'; (c) strip the form-check engines down to what survives the biomech audit — presence, rep count, hold-in-position seconds, gross position (torso line, horizontal check), start/stop timestamps — and remove side-specific pelvic cues from the verification path (they can remain as optional coaching, never as verification); (d) a generic 'timed hold in declared position' verifier so exercises not in the library (a physio's own Schroth exercise) can still be verified as presence + stillness + duration, keeping the instrument method-agnostic; (e) weekly adherence = verified minutes / prescribed minutes, shown alongside a 'reported' figure, with per-patient CSV export and REDCap-friendly column names. CLINICAL/VALIDATION: a concurrent-validity study in ~20–30 adults (founder's own population first): each home session simultaneously recorded on a second device and rated by two blinded physiotherapists for sets completed and seconds in position; report ICC(2,1) with 95% CI, Bland–Altman LoA, sensitivity/specificity for 'set completed', and false-verification rate (sloppy or sham reps counted as done) — this is the one number the product then puts on its front page. Then a test–retest of weekly verified minutes so 'adherence changed' is gated by an MDC the same way ATR is meant to be. DATA/GOVERNANCE: consent language covering camera-derived time-in-exercise (no video stored, landmarks only), data minimisation for minors, and an audit log so a trial can show the measure was not editable by the patient after the fact. PARTNERSHIPS: one exercise-trial PI (per docs/cuhk-approach.md) willing to run an adherence sub-study with an ethics amendment; one Schroth/SEAS clinic willing to prescribe through the app for 3 months so the instrument is validated on real PSSE content rather than the current library. COPY/CLAIMS: rewrite README, monthly page and Coach prompt to claim only adherence, pain, PSFS and endurance; remove 'progression', 'clinically meaningful', 'blocks contraindicated'.
proposals.biggest_risk: The measurement can be valid and still nobody buys it — and, worse, it can look valid and not be. Failure mode 1 (validity): a single webcam counts a rep or a hold whenever a landmark trace oscillates or goes still in roughly the right place; it cannot see whether the Schroth correction was actually held (elongation, concave-side breath, pelvic correction), so 'verified' means 'a body was in approximately this shape for N seconds', not 'the prescribed corrective was performed'. If the front page says 'verified adherence' and a trial later shows verified minutes do not predict outcome, the instrument is blamed rather than the exercise. Mitigation: name the construct honestly — 'camera-verified time in exercise position' — publish the false-verification rate from the observation study, and never let the Coach or PDF describe it as form quality. Failure mode 2 (adoption): the people who most need the number (trial PIs, clinics) are few, slow (ethics amendments, existing trials cannot add an instrument), and may prefer their own diary data precisely because it flatters adherence; patients may reject being watched, and physios may read the verified/reported gap as surveillance of their patients. If the first PI says no and no clinic prescribes through it, the feature is an internal analytics table with no external user. Failure mode 3 (scope creep back into the spine): the temptation to bolt 'and here is how your curve responded' onto the adherence report reintroduces every claim the audit killed.
proposals.evidence_basis: HIGH confidence, from the embedded digest and repo: the audit leaves adherence/pain/PSFS/endurance as the only honest claim space; formCheck rep-count and hold-timer primitives exist; exercises_completed lacks provenance and mixes chat self-report with camera data (lib/agents/tools.ts log_exercise, lib/agents/context.ts:31); docs/cuhk-approach.md lines 21–56 already frame the product as an adherence instrument for an exercise trial. MEDIUM confidence (from the digest's evidence findings, not re-verified by me against sources this run): PSSE trials with Cobb effects prescribed 30–45 min/day home dose (Schreiber 2015/2016; Yuan 2025 at 30 min/day, >=5 d/wk) and measured adherence by self-report; the biomech triage that rep counting, hold timing and side-plank line checks are plausible from one camera while L/R pelvic checks are not. LOW confidence / unverified: that any published smartphone or webcam system has reported ICC and LoA for home exercise time-in-position against direct observation in a scoliosis population — I could not check this and it should be searched before writing the validation protocol; if such a validated system exists, the differentiator becomes prescription-linked denominator plus method-agnostic verification rather than novelty of the measure. No citations, DOIs or numbers beyond those in the digest are asserted.
proposals.time_to_first_value: 4–6 weeks to an internal first value: prescription snapshot, provenance-flagged adherence events, verified-vs-reported weekly figure and CSV export, with the founder as patient zero and one physio reading the report. 3–4 months to the first external value: a 20–30-adult concurrent-validity study (dual-recording, two blinded raters) producing the ICC/LoA/false-verification figures that make the instrument quotable, plus a Schroth or SEAS clinic prescribing through the app. 9–12 months to the 100x moment: an adherence sub-study attached to an existing PSSE trial via ethics amendment, at which point the product is the named adherence instrument in a registered trial rather than a consumer app.

scores.title: The Signed Prescription Loop: physio-authored programme in, verified-dose ledger out
scores.reasoning: This is the only proposal that answers all four of my tests at once. Defensibility: it deletes the product's liability surface (algorithm-as-prescriber) and replaces it with a stored, versioned, clinician-signed prescription plus a verified-dose ledger; the moat is the accumulating prescription-vs-delivery dataset, not the exercise library. Distribution: the physio enrolls the patient in the room, which is the only acquisition channel in digital MSK that has ever worked without burning venture money on CAC (Hinge, Sword and Kaia all ended up selling to a payer/employer because D2C MSK never paid back). Who pays: per-clinician seat is the right unit; PSSE clinics in HK are private-pay and already bill for home programmes they cannot see, so a visibility tool is a small, defensible add-on to an existing cash flow. Buildability: honest 8-12 weeks, and the repo confirms the substrate (parse-program, physio_cleared mode, liaison route, care-team skeleton, form-check engines). Where I dock points: the 50-200 patients/physio figure is unverified and I have seen this exact 'clinicians will author in 5 minutes' promise die at the second patient; the SaMD boundary is real and unbudgeted; and a solo founder shipping a two-sided product (clinician auth, multi-tenant, RLS, PDF, CSV) in 6 months has no slack. Still the best risk-adjusted bet by a clear margin.

scores.title: Physio-Recorded Home Programme with a Weekly Verified Review Loop
scores.reasoning: Same thesis as the winner with one genuinely brilliant graft (the physio's own voice and clip on the patient's body) and one fatal add-on (clinic-side video capture plus weekly clinician review). The retention mechanism is the strongest of the five; accountability to a named person is the only home-exercise adherence story I have seen hold past week 12. But it makes the physio the bottleneck twice: recording in the room and reviewing on Sunday, both unpaid. Every 'clinician-in-the-loop weekly review' product I have funded has collapsed to the reviewers ignoring the queue. Storing video of adolescents' backs also makes the HK school cohort an ethics-board problem before it is a product problem, and the founder has no privacy counsel. As a standalone, too dependent on clinician behaviour; as a feature set to graft, excellent.

scores.title: Verified-Dose Adherence Instrument (trial-grade prescription-vs-delivery ledger with statistician export)
scores.reasoning: Technically the most honest and the cheapest to build (2 weeks to internal value, 6-8 to pitch), and the engineering spec (provenance enum, snapshot table, CSV + data dictionary) is exactly what the winner needs under the hood. But as a business it is a research-tools company selling to a handful of PIs with 6-18 month ethics cycles and study budgets that are already committed; CUHK's exercise trial may well be closed to recruitment, which the proposal itself concedes it could not verify. Trial instruments are a services revenue line, not a venture outcome, and they do not compound; the dataset only becomes valuable if a clinic channel feeds it patients continuously, which this proposal lacks. Right architecture, wrong customer as the primary.

scores.title: The Observation Ledger: own the six-month gap between school-screening visits
scores.reasoning: The biggest TAM argument in the set and I would have wanted to believe it five years ago. Now I do not. Distribution runs through the Department of Health Student Health Service, which the proposal admits is a 12-24 month horizon and which a solo founder with no clinical licence and unresolved employer IP will not move. Nobody pays: parents of children told 'your curve is small, come back in six months' are not a paying segment, DH will not procure from a pre-revenue founder, and clinics have no budget line for observation-arm monitoring. The risk profile is the worst of the five: the product's single output ('no change larger than your noise') sits right on top of the false-reassurance hazard the team's own strategy doc names, in minors, with a state agency adjacent. Helper-placed phone ATR with a 3-4 degree MDC cannot see the 5-10 degree growth-spurt progression that is the entire clinical point. Great pilot study, not a company, and not buildable to a paying state in 6 months.

scores.title: Verified Dose: a validated home dosimeter for prescribed scoliosis exercise
scores.reasoning: The purest version of 'stop claiming anything about the spine' and its method-agnostic generic hold verifier is a smart, cheap primitive. The concurrent-validity study with two blinded raters is the right scientific move and the proposal is candid that 'verified' means 'body approximately in shape for N seconds'. But it is a measurement without a buyer: it names trial PIs and clinics as customers without giving either an enrollment mechanism, a clinician surface, or a reason to author the denominator. A dosimeter with no prescribing channel is an analytics table. Its own biggest-risk section says as much. Overlaps ~80% with proposal 3 and both are subsumed by the winner's ledger.

judgements.winner: The Signed Prescription Loop: physio-authored programme in, verified-dose ledger out
judgements.graft_from_others: Three grafts, in priority order. (1) From the Physio-Recorded Home Programme: the physio's own voice as the cue. Do not do video. At authoring time, after the clinician confirms an exercise, let them record a 10-second audio cue on their phone; the patient hears their physio, not the LLM's TTS. That captures most of the accountability/relationship effect at near-zero clinician time, no video-of-minors exposure, and it kills lib/tts.ts and the invented-cue problem in one move. Skip the Sunday review queue; replace it with the winner's one-page digest and a single 'nothing to change / re-record this cue' tap. (2) From the Verified-Dose Adherence Instrument: its exact data model and its discipline. Ship the adherence_events and prescription_snapshots tables with append-only semantics, the provenance enum (form_check_verified | timer_only | chat_self_report | manual), landmark traces not video, and the CSV + data dictionary export from day one, even though no PI will use it for a year; that is what turns the clinic product into a dataset asset and keeps the trial route open without making it the business. Also take its 'study mode' flag: self_guided off, LLM cues off, scan numbers off. (3) From the home dosimeter: the generic 'timed hold in declared position' verifier so a Schroth or SEAS physio's own exercises (not in the library) still produce verified minutes, keeping the loop method-agnostic; and the rule that the front page names the construct honestly as 'camera-verified time in exercise position', never form quality. Run its 20-30 session blinded-rater check before the word 'verified' appears in any clinician digest. Explicitly do not graft anything from the Observation Ledger except the ATR sign/orientation and sweep fixes and the 'Not sure' answer everywhere; keep the adolescent screening cohort out of scope until an adult clinic pilot is paying. Sequencing for the solo founder: weeks 1-3 clinical fixes and retire self_guided asymmetric cues, cascade.ts, inferStiffHipFlexorSide; weeks 3-8 clinician account + authoring over parse-program + audio cue + snapshot/event tables; weeks 8-12 digest, CSV, blinded-rater check, one design-partner clinic. Get a written SaMD opinion in parallel; the defensible line is that every clinical decision is the clinician's and the app is delivery and record.

scores.title: The Signed Prescription Loop: physio-authored programme in, verified-dose ledger out
scores.reasoning: This is the only proposal that matches how PSSE actually works and what the evidence actually supports. SOSORT's position is that PSSE is a clinician-delivered, individually prescribed intervention; the ingredient that Yuan 2025 (as summarised in the digest, confidence medium) isolated was clinician-prescribed content plus remote supervision, not an app choosing exercises. Moving authorship to a named licensed physio retires, in one move, every finding in the audit I would refuse to sign off on: the backwards waist fold, the founder's fold-left leakage, the Fishman 'absolute' side-plank rule, the invented cascades, X-ray laterality flips, and the 'which way does your back bulge' guessing that inverts every side cue for lumbar patterns. As a clinician I would prescribe THIS to my own patients because it is my prescription; I would not prescribe the current self-guided library to anyone. It also solves my real problem, which is that I have zero visibility of the 30-45 min/day home dose between visits. Deductions: 'verified' from a single webcam is only defensible for rep counts, hold-in-position time and side-plank line; the proposal correctly restricts to those, but the observer-agreement study is still unrun, and a wrong 'verified' number in my chart is worse than a diary. The SaMD boundary needs a regulatory opinion before paid launch. Self-guided fallback must be strictly symmetric Tier 4-5 and disabled under 18.

scores.title: Physio-Recorded Home Programme with a Weekly Verified Review Loop
scores.reasoning: Clinically this is the most faithful to real Schroth/SEAS home practice: we already teach the correction on the patient's own body and many of us send WhatsApp clips because nothing else transfers the individual correction reliably. Recording the cue on the patient's body eliminates the concave/convex convention problem entirely, since there is no side-keyed text to get wrong, and the physio's own voice is a genuine adherence lever that a chatbot persona is not (general home-exercise-adherence knowledge, confidence medium). The weekly review with a default 'nothing to change' is exactly the supervision loop the digital-PSSE trial used. Why it scores below Proposal 1: the physio is a hard bottleneck (unpaid Sunday review, 90 s capture per exercise in a 30-minute slot), video of adolescents' backs is a safeguarding exposure that will be judged before any clinical merit, and it puts less weight on the structured dose denominator and provenance that make the adherence data usable for a clinic audit or trial. Best treated as the cue-delivery layer of Proposal 1 rather than a rival.

scores.title: Verified-Dose Adherence Instrument (trial-grade prescription-vs-delivery ledger with statistician export)
scores.reasoning: The methodological argument is correct: every PSSE trial has an unmeasured independent variable and per-protocol analysis needs a dose denominator. But from a clinician's chair this is a research instrument, not something I prescribe to a patient; the customer is a small number of PIs with 6-18 month ethics cycles, and the founder has no revenue or patient benefit while waiting. It also leaves the clinical content question unanswered for anyone outside a study. The engineering (append-only adherence_events, prescription snapshots, three-tier provenance, study-mode flag, data dictionary) is exactly right and should be built regardless, which is why it scores above the midpoint, but as THE feature it optimises for the statistician rather than for the patient or the treating physio. Risk that the 'verified' bit is theatre is identical to Proposal 1 and is candidly stated.

scores.title: The Observation Ledger: own the six-month gap between school-screening visits
scores.reasoning: The gap is real and the cohort arithmetic is broadly right, but the proposal asks a parent-placed phone to do a job it cannot do safely. Helper-placed ATR will have an MDC of several degrees and ATR-Cobb correlation is only moderate, so a 5-10 degree Cobb progression across peak height velocity can sit entirely inside the noise; a parent reading 'no change larger than your noise' will hear 'stable' no matter how the copy is written. That is the one false-reassurance hazard the team's own strategy doc names, scaled to tens of thousands of children with the Department of Health's name next to it. The growth-velocity and maturity capture, HK jurisdiction thresholds, and the bracing-window prompt are genuinely valuable and missing from the product today. But the DH channel is a multi-year horizon, the pilot depends on a clinic observation arm agreeing to a phone next to Scolioscan, and it abandons the exercise product the founder actually has. I would support it as an adolescent intake module, not as the company.

scores.title: Verified Dose: a validated home dosimeter for prescribed scoliosis exercise
scores.reasoning: Honest and disciplined: it names the construct correctly ('camera-verified time in exercise position', not form quality), proposes the concurrent-validity study with two blinded raters, ICC(2,1), Bland-Altman and a false-verification rate, and is method-agnostic via a generic timed-hold verifier so a real Schroth exercise can be verified without living in the library. Those are the right clinical-measurement instincts. What it lacks is the prescriber loop: it measures dose without owning who set it or who reviews it, so like Proposal 3 the end user is a PI or an analytics table rather than a patient and their physio, and adoption failure mode 2 (nobody buys a valid number) is stated by the proposal itself. The scope-creep risk back into spine claims is well identified. Strong as a component; weaker as the single feature.

judgements.winner: The Signed Prescription Loop: physio-authored programme in, verified-dose ledger out
judgements.graft_from_others:
From Proposal 2: make the physio's recorded clip and spoken cue (Cantonese or English) on the patient's own body the primary cue medium inside the signed prescription, with typed side/dose as the structured metadata beneath it. This removes the concave/convex text convention from the patient-facing path entirely and is how PSSE clinics already transfer corrections. Keep the weekly three-minute review screen with a default 'seen, keep going' and a one-tap 're-record this cue'. Adults first; no minor's video leaves the device without guardian consent, with a text-plus-audio fallback.

From Proposal 5: the generic 'timed hold in declared position' verifier so any physio-authored exercise outside the library can be verified as presence plus stillness plus duration; the honest construct name 'camera-verified time in exercise position' (never 'form quality'); and the concurrent-validity protocol (20-30 adults, dual recording, two blinded physio raters, ICC(2,1) with 95% CI, Bland-Altman LoA, sensitivity/specificity for 'set completed', false-verification rate) run before the word 'verified' appears in any clinician digest.

From Proposal 3: the append-only adherence_events and prescription_snapshots tables with RLS, three-tier provenance reported separately (camera-verified, timer-only, self-reported), the study-mode flag that locks the exercise list to the prescription and disables self-guided selection, LLM-invented cues, posture-scan numbers and cascade copy, and the CSV plus data dictionary export keyed by study code. Build it now so the clinic pilot doubles as the dataset a CUHK investigator can later adopt.

From Proposal 4: the adolescent intake block (date of birth, sex, menarche status, recent growth spurt, Risser/Cobb from report, brace hours) and the fixed bracing-window copy for Cobb >=20 degrees with growth remaining; jurisdiction-configured ATR thresholds with the HK pathway described accurately (verify Luk 2010 / Fong 2015 before shipping copy); ATR measured at the physio-nominated apex level and reported per level, gated on per-user MDC; and the hard rule that the product never emits 'stable', 'improving', 'drift' or 'progression' for anything other than a radiologist-measured Cobb.

Before any clinician sees the library: fix sitting_waist_fold direction, rewrite childs_pose_side_reach rationale, downgrade side-plank side and the five 'absolute' rules to ask_physio, delete cascade.ts and inferStiffHipFlexorSide, add the fusion/osteoporosis/pregnancy/connective-tissue intake, and wire the ongoing red-flag screen and chat pre-classifier. A Schroth- or SEAS-certified physio should sign off the authoring vocabulary and the 'verified' definition, and a regulatory opinion on the SaMD boundary is on the critical path before a paid launch.
